newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer as LME tightness worsens.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer as LME tightness worsens.

text.p: COMEX copper ended firmer Monday, the advance helped by a doubling of the backwardation on LME as the much expected nearby squeeze began to bite hard, dealers said.
A further rebound on COMEX was also due after the sharp selloff last week, traders said.
Much of the focus in copper was on LME's so-called third Wednesday pricing on Monday which, combined with an already strong backwardation, prompted heavy cash buying on LME, dealers said.
September COMEX copper settled 2.00 cents firmer at 106.30 cents a lb, traded 106.90 to 105.40 cents. Spot July went out 2.15 cents higher at 110.20 cents.
The LME cash to three months backwardation ended at $250/$270 a tonne, doubled from Friday's close because of the Third Wednesday pricing and nearby tightness.
A backwardation is usually a sign of tightness in supply.
But the tightness comes despite LME stocks continuing to rise during the summer seasonal slowdown in the northern hemisphere.
LME stocks rose 2,075 tonnes to 141,200 tonnes.
"The whole issue is concentrated around the cash backwardation in London, and the tightness in July for the next two weeks," Fred Demler of E D & F Man International said.
It appeared that some of the tightness was being rolled forward into August but not much further, Demler added.

COMEX stocks fell 2,379 short tons Monday to 33,075 short tons as metal flowed from the New York exchange into warehouses holding LME warranted copper on the U.S. West Coast from arbitrage deals, dealers said.
More metal was expected to flow in the same direction over the coming sessions.
